title: Science of Superpowers
subtitle: Pop Quiz
speaker: Ms Sparks
intro: Surprise. Everything from this week, right now.
Twelve seconds a question. I did warn you on Monday.

questions.prompt:
In the cell model from Monday's lab,
what does a laser actually do to a cell?
questions.explainRight: Correct. The beam changes its state, it doesn't break it.
questions.explainWrong: It changes what the cell can do. That's the whole point of the lab.

questions.prompt:
A strength-boosted cell pushes a block into a wall.
What happens?
options: The block stops at the wall
questions.explainRight: Right. A boost is not an excuse to ignore a wall.
questions.explainWrong: The block stops. Strength doesn't make a wall optional.

questions.prompt:
A prism is in the path of a beam.
What comes out the other side?
options: Two beams of a new colour
questions.explainWrong: It redirects the beam. Same beam, different direction.

questions.prompt:
Why does a boosted state wear off
instead of lasting forever?
options: The cell runs out of the energy holding it
Only if the cell is hit again
It lasts until the end of the lesson
questions.explainRight: Correct. Nothing holds a borrowed state for free.
questions.explainWrong: It costs energy to hold, and the energy runs out.

questions.prompt: What is the safest way to test an unfamiliar power?
options: In a crowd, so there is help nearby
In a controlled lab, with a reset to hand
questions.explainRight: Exactly. Control the room and you can afford a mistake.
questions.explainWrong: In a lab, where you can reset. That's why we have the labs.

questions.prompt:
Two powers meet and cancel out.
What does that tell you?
options: They act on the same thing in opposite ways
questions.explainRight: Good. Cancelling means they share a mechanism.
questions.explainWrong: They work on the same thing, pulling opposite ways.

outro: Papers in. I'll have these back to you Monday.
Enjoy your weekend. Some of you have reading to do.
